title: The ten days, lived
hookLine: one small change each day between the holy days
tomorrow: Saba wants to fast on Yom Kippur. his doctor says no. who wins?

cards: Office hours: Tuesdays, two to four. Plenty of people can only be reached at certain times. But Isaiah says something odd about God: "Seek ye the LORD while He may be found, call ye upon Him while He is near."
While? Isn't God supposed to be findable always? The rabbis caught the oddness too, and their answer puts a window on the calendar.

teach.b: In the Talmud, the rabbis read Isaiah's line as pointing to these days: the ten days from Rosh Hashanah to Yom Kippur, called the ten days of return. Near always, their reading goes, but in this stretch, nearer.

teach.h: RETURN IS GOOD ALWAYS, BETTER NOW.
teach.b: Maimonides says it plainly: return is good every day of the year, and in these ten days it's even better, and it's accepted at once. So the ten days aren't a waiting room between two holidays.
They're the window being open. And what do people do with an open window? Nothing huge.

teach.h: A SMALL CUSTOM, KEPT FOR A FEW DAYS.
teach.b: The Shulchan Aruch, the code of Jewish law, records a custom: someone who's usually relaxed about a certain food rule keeps it more carefully, just for these days.
Small, and a little odd: a stricter habit held for a short time. But that's the method.
One change, kept briefly, so you learn what it's like to be the person who does it. A softer word with a sibling. The phone out of the bedroom.
A call returned. One a day, and by Yom Kippur, ten of them.
A small change has the advantage of actually happening.

how: In the days between Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur, Jews often add a few extra prayers, give tzedakah, ask forgiveness from people they've hurt, and take on one small extra practice for the week.

games.q: you and your brother have been snapping at each other for weeks. it's the ten days. which move fits the method?
o: write him a long letter listing everything you'll fix this year.
one small thing: no sarcasm at dinner, starting tonight.
wait for Yom Kippur and make one big apology then.
games.why: the method is small and now: one change, held for a short time, while the window is open.

practice: For the sit, think through three things. One small change you could make tomorrow. The thing most likely to get in the way.
And the exact moment you'll do it instead: when I reach for my phone in bed, it goes on the dresser. Keep it small enough that calling it a change makes you smile.
